description: NaFeP₂O₇ crystallizes in the monoclinic P2₁ space group. Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ pentagonal pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one FeO₆ octahedra, corners with three PO₄ tetrahedra, edges with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra, and edges with two PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 51°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.57 Å. Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share  a cornercorner with one NaO₆ pentagonal pyramid, corners with six PO₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two equivalent NaO₆ pentagonal pyramids. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 2.01-2.07 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent FeO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent NaO₆ pentagonal pyramids,  a cornercorner with one PO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₆ pentagonal pyramid. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 38-49°. There are three shorter (1.53 Å) and one longer (1.64 Å) P-O bond length. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent FeO₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one NaO₆ pentagonal pyramid,  a cornercorner with one PO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₆ pentagonal pyramid. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 23-49°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.52-1.63 Å. There are seven inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a bent 150 degrees geometry to one Fe and one P atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na and two P atoms.
